body: Oprah Winfrey was born into poverty in rural Mississippi and faced numerous hardships including abuse and teenage pregnancy. She was fired from her first television job as an anchor. Despite these setbacks, she went on to become one of the most influential media moguls in history, building a billion-dollar empire and using her platform to inspire millions around the world.

J.K. Rowling was a single mother living on welfare, struggling with depression, and had her manuscript rejected by twelve publishers before Bloomsbury finally accepted Harry Potter. She went from being nearly homeless to becoming the first billionaire author in history, creating a literary phenomenon that changed childhood reading forever.

Walt Disney was fired from a newspaper for lacking imagination and had his first animation studio go bankrupt. He faced countless rejections and financial struggles before creating Mickey Mouse and building the Disney empire that continues to enchant generations.

Colonel Harland Sanders was 62 years old when he started Kentucky Fried Chicken. He had been rejected over 1,000 times before someone finally believed in his chicken recipe. His face now appears on KFC restaurants in over 150 countries.

Stephen King's first novel, Carrie, was rejected by 30 publishers. He threw the manuscript in the trash, but his wife retrieved it and encouraged him to keep trying. He has since published over 60 novels and sold more than 350 million copies.

Thomas Edison was told by teachers that he was too stupid to learn anything. He was fired from his first two jobs for being non-productive. Despite over 1,000 failed attempts at creating the light bulb, he persisted and changed the world.

Michael Jordan was cut from his high school basketball team. He went home and cried. He used that rejection as fuel to become the greatest basketball player of all time, winning six NBA championships and five MVP awards.

Albert Einstein did not speak until he was four and could not read until he was seven. His teachers considered him slow and mentally handicapped. He went on to develop the theory of relativity and won the Nobel Prize in Physics.

Steven Spielberg was rejected from the University of Southern California School of Theater, Film and Television three times. He eventually attended another school and dropped out to pursue directing. He is now one of the most successful filmmakers in history.

Vera Wang failed to make the U.S. Olympic figure skating team and was passed over for the editor-in-chief position at Vogue. At age 40, she started designing wedding gowns and built a billion-dollar fashion empire.

Sylvester Stallone was so broke he had to sell his dog for $25. He wrote the script for Rocky in three days and was offered $350,000 for it, but refused unless he could star in the film. The movie won three Academy Awards and launched his career.
The Beatles were rejected by Decca Records who said guitar groups were on the way out. They went on to become the best-selling music act of all time with over 600 million records sold worldwide.
Dr. Seuss's first book was rejected by 27 publishers. He is now one of the best-selling children's authors ever, with over 600 million copies sold.
Henry Ford went bankrupt five times before founding the Ford Motor Company. His assembly line innovation revolutionized manufacturing and made cars affordable for the average person.
Soichiro Honda was turned down for a job at Toyota and started making scooters in his shed. His company, Honda, is now one of the largest motorcycle and automobile manufacturers in the world.

Jack Ma applied to 30 different jobs and was rejected by all of them, including KFC where 24 people applied and 23 were hired—he was the only one rejected. He went on to found Alibaba, one of the world's largest e-commerce companies.
Milton Hershey started three candy companies that all failed before founding the Lancaster Caramel Company and eventually Hershey's Chocolate. His name is now synonymous with chocolate worldwide.
Akio Morita's first product, a rice cooker, burned rice and was a complete failure. He went on to co-found Sony and revolutionize consumer electronics.
Fred Smith wrote a paper at Yale outlining an overnight delivery service and received a C grade. He used that idea to found FedEx, which is now worth over $70 billion.
Howard Schultz grew up in a housing project in Brooklyn. He was rejected by banks 242 times before securing funding for Starbucks. He transformed a small coffee shop into a global empire.
Richard Branson has dyslexia and dropped out of school at 16. He started a magazine and then a record shop, eventually building the Virgin Group with over 400 companies.
Simon Cowell was fired from his job at EMI Music Publishing. He went on to create television shows like Pop Idol and The X Factor, becoming one of the most influential figures in entertainment.

body: Serena Williams grew up practicing on public courts in Compton, California. She and her sister Venus faced racism and skepticism but dominated women's tennis, winning 23 Grand Slam singles titles.
Simone Biles was placed in foster care as a child due to her mother's substance abuse. She was adopted by her grandparents and became the most decorated gymnast in history.
LeBron James was raised by a single mother in Akron, Ohio, and moved between apartments. He became one of the greatest basketball players of all time and a billionaire athlete.
Tiger Woods was introduced to golf before age two by his father. Despite personal setbacks and injuries, he became one of the most successful golfers in history.
Muhammad Ali was banned from boxing for refusing the draft during the Vietnam War. He returned to become the first three-time heavyweight champion and a global icon for civil rights.
Manny Pacquiao left home at 14 due to poverty and lived on the streets of Manila. He became the only eight-division world champion in boxing history.
Cristiano Ronaldo grew up in a working-class family in Madeira, Portugal. He became one of the greatest footballers of all time through relentless dedication.
Lionel Messi was diagnosed with growth hormone deficiency as a child. FC Barcelona paid for his treatment and he became one of the most decorated footballers ever.
Tom Brady was drafted 199th overall in the NFL and was the sixth quarterback taken. He went on to win seven Super Bowls, more than any franchise in history.
Michael Phelps was diagnosed with ADHD as a child and was bullied for his lisp and big ears. He became the most decorated Olympian of all time with 28 medals.
Usain Bolt grew up in a small town in Jamaica playing cricket and football. He became the fastest man in history and an eight-time Olympic gold medalist.
Katie Ledecky was the youngest swimmer on the U.S. Olympic team at 15. She went on to win seven Olympic gold medals and set multiple world records.
Simone Manuel became the first African American woman to win an individual Olympic gold medal in swimming, breaking barriers in a historically segregated sport.
Ibtihaj Muhammad faced discrimination as a Muslim fencer wearing hijab. She became the first Muslim American woman to wear hijab while competing for the U.S. at the Olympics.
Yusra Mardini was a Syrian refugee who swam for three hours in the Aegean Sea to push a sinking boat to safety. She competed on the first Refugee Olympic Team.
Tegla Loroupe grew up in poverty in Kenya and ran barefoot. She became the first African woman to win the New York City Marathon.
Wilma Rudolph was born prematurely and contracted polio, scarlet fever, and pneumonia as a child. She became the first American woman to win three gold medals in track and field at a single Olympics.
Bethany Hamilton lost her left arm in a shark attack at age 13. She returned to professional surfing just one month later and continues to compete.
Derek Redmond tore his hamstring during the 1992 Olympics 400m semifinal. His father helped him finish the race, creating one of the most iconic moments in Olympic history.
Jesse Owens won four gold medals at the 1936 Berlin Olympics in front of Adolf Hitler, disproving Nazi theories of racial superiority.
Jackie Robinson broke Major League Baseball's color barrier in 1947, facing death threats and abuse while becoming Rookie of the Year.
Hank Aaron broke Babe Ruth's home run record while facing racist threats. He finished with 755 home runs and became a civil rights icon.
Roberto Clemente was a Puerto Rican baseball player who faced discrimination. He became the first Latin American player inducted into the Baseball Hall of Fame.
Fernando Valenzuela was a teenage pitcher from Mexico who became a cultural phenomenon with the Dodgers in the 1980s.
Ichiro Suzuki was told he was too small for American baseball. He became one of the greatest hitters in MLB history.
Shohei Ohtani became the first player in MLB history to be named an All-Star as both a pitcher and hitter in the same season.
Megan Rapinoe grew up in a conservative town and came out publicly as gay. She became a World Cup champion and advocate for equal pay.
Alex Morgan faced rejection from youth teams before becoming one of the most prolific goal scorers in U.S. soccer history.
Carli Lloyd was cut from her youth national team multiple times before scoring a hat trick in the 2015 World Cup final.
Mia Hamm was the youngest player on the U.S. women's national team at 15. She became one of the greatest female athletes of all time.
Abby Wambach struggled with addiction and identity before becoming the all-time leading scorer for the U.S. women's national team.
Hope Solo faced a difficult childhood and became one of the greatest goalkeepers in women's soccer history.
Julie Foudy was told girls shouldn't play sports. She became a two-time World Cup champion and Olympic gold medalist.
Brandi Chastain scored the winning penalty in the 1999 World Cup final, creating one of the most iconic moments in sports history.
Michelle Akers battled chronic fatigue syndrome while becoming one of the greatest players in women's soccer history.
